LESSON: ARTICULATION OF WORDS AND SIGNING VOCABULARY (PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY)

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.1: Articulation of words and signing vocabulary (Pronunciation and vocabulary)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Articulation of words and signing vocabulary (Pronunciation and vocabulary), part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: What should we do to improve our reading speed? 2. Why should we show the right feelings when reading a text?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Articulation of words and signing vocabulary (Pronunciation and vocabulary) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: confidence and self-esteem as the learner is able to read fluently.

● Communication and collaboration: Teamwork as learners take turns to sign read at an appropriate speed as modelled by the teacher or peers

Values:
Unity: Cooperation as the learner take turns to read a text at an appropriate speed with peers

122

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Citizenship: Social cohesion as the learner plays a word ladder game with peers.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Sign Reading fluency is emphasised in Indigenous Language Activities..
